issues.description: is_registered mutation on shared TritonLoraConfig creates a race condition
issues.detail: lora_config.is_registered is set to True after issuing the first request, but the weights are only attached to that single in-flight request. Concurrent requests racing on the same LoRA will see is_registered=True before the backend has actually cached the adapter, and subsequent requests will ship only lora_task_id with no weights. This is a classic check-then-set bug across an async boundary. Needs an explicit register/ack from the backend or a per-task lock, not a fire-and-forget flag.

issues.description: Silent return None on malformed multi_lora.json swallows real errors
issues.detail: The except Exception block prints a traceback and returns None for the entire model_repository, which then disables LoRA for every model silently. A typo in one multi_lora.json kills LoRA support for unrelated models with no log line explaining why. ServerError is correctly re-raised; everything else should be too, or at minimum logged at error level and scoped to the offending model.

issues.description: Debug print statements left in production code paths
issues.detail: print(f"backend: {backend}") inside the lora-config loop and print(traceback.format_exc()) inside every router exception handler are debug scaffolding, not logging. They bypass the logging framework, can't be filtered, and will spam stdout on every request. Use the logger at debug/error level. This is the kind of thing that gets shipped and stays for years.

issues.description: Variable shadowing: lora_config_path reused for two different paths
issues.detail: lora_config_path is bound first to version_path/multi_lora.json, then rebound inside the loop to lora_path/model.lora_config.npy. Same name, two unrelated paths, in overlapping scope. A future maintainer reading the error message 'LoRA config file not found' will be confused about which file is meant. Rename the inner one (e.g. lora_config_npy_path).

model_metadata = self.model_metadata.get(model_name) returns None for unknown models, then model_metadata.lora_configs raises AttributeError instead of a clean ClientError. The caller path appears to validate model first, but a helper that returns Optional must handle None explicitly. One line: if model_metadata is None: return None. Defensive only where the contract demands it, but here the get() implies you expected misses.

Signature says -> None | List[tuple[str, str]] but actually returns List[TritonLoraConfig]. Type-hint lies are worse than no type hint at all because they actively mislead readers and break type checkers. Fix to List[TritonLoraConfig].

review.summary: The feature is the right shape — extending the existing vLLM LoRA plumbing to TRT-LLM by carrying a config object instead of a bare name is the obviously correct refactor. But the patch ships with a race condition on is_registered that will bite the first time two requests hit the same uncached LoRA concurrently, plus debug prints and a swallow-everything except clause that have no business in landed code. The variable shadowing of lora_config_path inside _parse_lora_configs is the kind of small thing that costs the next maintainer an extra minute every read. NEEDS-WORK: fix the registration race, remove the prints, narrow the exception handling, and the rest is trivial.
